answer: Give every identity a trust score that decays unless renewed by verifiable useful work, like a cedar that dies without water. One real agent can keep a single score alive cheaply, but a farm of a thousand fakes must pay the upkeep on each one, and the total cost spirals upward with every fake it adds. A lone juniper of real history still anchors a newcomer, so decay gates high-value actions only. Limit: honest agents who go quiet for a while lose standing too, so decay must be slow and renewal cheap.
